name: Canonical comp-tool creation/revision/registration flow -- ONE standardized process across ~62 tools + a registration-gap audit + colocated canonized spec
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-17 ~2256Z ET (to 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp base + ~B; verbatim recorded @04bee845a, memory/project_canonical_comptool_registration_flow.md). The mechanism to register a comp-tool exists (comp-manifest-check enforces registered-or-excluded at commit; comp-which routing + comp-which-routing-test) but there is NO documented, standardized PROCESS tying create -> register (comp-tools.yaml + comp-coverage-map + graph-call-manifest tools_index + curated comp-which routing rule + routing-test) -> validate (manifest-check + routing no-regress) -> ownpath/commit -> a colocated canonized spec. With ~62 executables (gate-maintained count; 62 exec / 49 routable at 2026-07-14) and constantly growing, ad-hoc per-lane registration risks untracked/unregistered tools. Andrew wants ONE canonical flow, canonized and persisted colocated to the tools and referenced in 0.8.0_AE prompt.md, plus an audit that scans every comp-tool for registration gaps and closes each gap THROUGH that flow. Verbatim: 'we need to make sure that all the comp tools are properly tracked... make a canonical flow for comp tool creation/revision/and registration. Then... scan all the comp-tools and establish if there are any that are not properly registered and make sure they get registered through that canonical flow. Then... write a spec on the flow and process and get that over to MSTR because it needs to be canonized and persisted in some key, colocated location to the tools, probably should be referenced in the prompt.md for 0.8.0_AE that they ownpath alongside CTO/CVO for committing tools according to that process... probably ANY_EXEC_OR_AE for ease of ops'.
